18 An object of weight 15.0 N is pulled along a horizontal surface at a constant velocity of 2.00 m s–1.
The force pulling the object is 12.0 N at 30.0 to the horizontal, as shown.
2.00 m s–1
12.0 N
30.0
15.0 N
What is the power used to move the object?
A
12.0 W
B
20.8 W
C
24.0 W
D
30.0 W

hints: Notice the $12.0 \text{ N}$ pull is at $30.0^{\circ}$ to the $2.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ horizontal velocity, so only part of the force acts along the motion.
Recall power for a constant force is $P = Fv\cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between force and velocity, here $30.0^{\circ}$.
First calculate the horizontal component $12.0\cos 30.0^{\circ}$, then multiply by $2.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to get power in $\text{W}$.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: the object moves horizontally at $v = 2.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so only the horizontal component of the $12.0 \text{ N}$ force does work.
State the rule for power with an angled force: $P = Fv\cos\theta$, where $\theta = 30.0^{\circ}$ is the angle between the force and the velocity.
Resolve the pulling force along the motion: $F_{horizontal} = F\cos\theta = 12.0 \times \cos 30.0^{\circ}$.
Multiply by velocity for power: $P = 10.39 \times 2.00 = 20.78 \text{ W}$, which is $20.8 \text{ W}$ to 3 significant figures with unit $\text{W}$.
The $15.0 \text{ N}$ weight is vertical and perpendicular to motion, so it contributes no power. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is $12.0 \times \sin 30.0^{\circ} \times 2.00 = 12.0 \text{ W}$, the power from the vertical component which does no work for horizontal motion.

B.explanation: This is $12.0 \cos 30.0^{\circ} \times 2.00 = 20.8 \text{ W}$, the horizontal force component times the horizontal velocity.

C.explanation: This is $12.0 \times 2.00 = 24.0 \text{ W}$, which ignores the $30.0^{\circ}$ angle and uses the full pulling force.

D.explanation: This is $15.0 \times 2.00 = 30.0 \text{ W}$, which uses the $15.0 \text{ N}$ weight acting vertically with no displacement in its direction.
